background_sections.adjustment: He's rebuilt his life three times, and he says this is simply the fourth, without any self-pity. He adjusted better than almost anyone, because he knew the shape of it. He'll tell you that the first time you lose everything it destroys you, the second time it's merely very hard, and the third time you find you have a method. He doesn't offer this as wisdom, only as information, to people who look like they need it.
background_sections.forward: Nizar is searching for Hala, town by town and list by list, in a notebook with dates, in a way that's painful to watch. He's also started teaching again, mathematics for four children at a trading post in Booty Bay, in the evenings, for nothing. He says it's to keep his hand in. His English is careful and a little old-fashioned, learned from books and the radio.
background_sections.now: He travels aboard the Crossing, the ship between Booty Bay and the other continent, because from there he can reach the most towns. In a party he stays at the back, holding the order of things together while the front rank works. His father's watch runs backwards on its chain. He's never had it mended, and he winds it every morning regardless.

recruits.look: Syrian man in his early 40s, tall and very upright, black hair greying at the sides, neat beard, dark eyes, deep laugh lines. Pale sand and deep teal robes with layered geometric trim, a staff of slowly counter-rotating brass rings, faint afterimages trailing his hands. A pocket watch with a cracked crystal, running backwards, on a fine chain.

recruits.name: Yusuf Al-Rawi
recruits.backstory: A pharmacist in Basra for nineteen years, in a shop where half the job was medicine and the other half was listening to people with no money for a doctor. He knows doses and he knows poisons. He's very warm, and he won't sugarcoat anything for you.
recruits.greeting: Sit, sit, please. You're not dying, I can see that from here. But you'll sit anyway, because I'm older than you.

background_sections.before:
A counter, a wall of drawers, and a queue that was also a social occasion.

A wife, Suhad, three sons and a daughter, and a house with too many people in it and a flat roof they all slept on in the summer. He talks about them easily and often, in the present tense, and nobody's heard him guess at where they are.
background_sections.adjustment:
He was calm about it. He found the work and did it, the way he'd found work in two other countries already.

He's one of the very few here who says plainly that he expects to see his family again, and he says it so calmly that people believe him.
background_sections.forward:
A proper dispensary, with shelves, drawers and labels, and somebody trained to run it when he's out.

He's teaching two people to read the labels he writes, so the place can keep going without him.
background_sections.now:
The Bloodsail Anchorage, where the pressed crews and prisoners are sick and nobody else will treat them. The pirates put up with him because he treats them too.

In a party he's at the back with a bandolier of vials, dosing by eye and not by guess. The brass counting tray is strapped flat on his back, and his numbers are always right.

recruits.look: Iraqi man in his early 40s, broad and heavy-set but light on his feet, black hair receding and swept back, thick moustache and short beard. Dark green and gold robes with wide sleeves, a serpent-carved stave, corked vials in a bandolier across his chest. A pharmacist's scratched brass pill-counting tray slung flat at his back.

recruits.name: Rhys Morgan
recruits.backstory: Rhys flew hawks at weddings in the Brecon Beacons, which paid better than you'd think and was mostly about keeping a bird calm in front of two hundred people in hats. He had Tegan on his glove the evening the world changed, and she crossed over with him. He's quiet, patient and quick to laugh once he's decided you're all right, and he trusts the hawk's opinion of a stranger more than his own.
recruits.greeting: Keep your voice down near the trees, would you? She hunts better when nobody's chattering at her.

background_sections.before: Rhys flew hawks at weddings in the Brecon Beacons, which paid better than you'd think and was mostly about keeping a bird calm in front of two hundred people in hats. He worked out of a falconry centre outside Brecon, doing weddings in the summer and school visits in the winter. His mam ran the cafe at the centre and called every bird by the wrong name on purpose. He had his hawk Tegan on his glove the evening the world changed.
background_sections.adjustment: Tegan crossed over with him, and she adjusted much faster than he did. She caught her first hare in Stonetalon within a week, and he decided that if she could manage, so could he. He still checks the sky for weather the way he did at home, and here he's usually right. He's quiet and patient, and quick to laugh once he's decided you're all right.
background_sections.forward: Rhys wants to get word to Brecon, or else find out there's no Brecon to send it to. He's not sure which answer frightens him more. Until then, he'll keep teaching the boy. He's started to think Tegan might choose the boy one day, and he's surprised how much that pleases him.
background_sections.now: He hunts the western ridges of Stonetalon, where the game is good and the road is quiet. Tegan sits on his arm while he talks, and watches whoever he's talking to. He trusts her opinion of a stranger more than his own. He's teaching a tauren boy from Sun Rock Retreat how to hold a glove, and the boy is better at it than Rhys was at that age.

recruits.look: Welsh man, 30, lean and athletic, dark brown wavy hair cut short, light stubble, grey-green eyes. Green and brown ranger leathers with a short hooded cloak, a longbow, a hunting horn, a hawk on a leather gauntlet, a falconer's swivel and bell on a cord round his wrist.

recruits.name: Gunnar Sigurðsson
recruits.backstory: Gunnar brewed beer in Akureyri, in a shed behind his uncle's garage that grew into a proper brewery with a queue out the door on Fridays. He's enormous, loud and generous, and he took to the barbarians of the north the moment he met them, because anyone who toasts their ancestors before a fight has the right idea about both. He still carries a hydrometer, and he still uses it.
recruits.greeting: You look like someone who's had a long road. Sit down, I've got something you should try.

background_sections.before: Gunnar brewed beer in Akureyri, in the north of Iceland, starting in a shed behind his uncle's garage and growing it into a proper brewery with a queue out the door on Fridays. He had a dog called Bruno and a long-running argument with his sister about whether stout counts as food. He played second row for a rugby club that lost almost every match and celebrated every one anyway. He still carries his hydrometer, and he still uses it.
background_sections.adjustment: He landed in snow in the far north, which helped, because snow was the one thing that felt normal. A barbarian clan took him in after he fixed their mead, and he's been fixing it ever since. Anyone who toasts their ancestors before a fight, he says, has the right idea about both. He cried the first time he heard their ancestor songs, and he doesn't care who knows it.
background_sections.forward: Gunnar wants to find a barley that will grow on the Arathi moor, because what's in Hammerfall's stores isn't fit for pigs. After that he'd like to brew something good enough that the orcs stop pretending they don't like it. He's close, he says. He's been saying that for a year.
background_sections.now: He's in Hammerfall now, usually by the inn, swapping recipes with Grettha and losing most of the arguments. He's enormous, loud and generous, and he'll press a drink on anyone who looks like they've had a long road. The keg on his back is never quite empty. Nobody has ever seen him fill it.

recruits.look: Icelandic man, 37, very big and broad, long dark-blond hair tied back, a thick braided beard, pale blue eyes. Fur-trimmed barbarian hides over mail, a two-handed axe across his back and a small wooden keg on a strap, a brass hydrometer in a leather sleeve on his belt.

recruits.name: Réka Farkas
recruits.backstory: Réka made stop-motion films in Budapest, moving puppets one frame at a time until they looked alive. She'd done it for twelve years when the worlds joined, and it turned out to be the best training for necromancy anyone's ever had. She's sly, funny and very precise, and she treats the dead the way she treated her puppets, with patience and a lot of small adjustments.
recruits.greeting: Please don't stare at the crow, it's shy. Well, it used to be shy, and now it's mostly bones and opinions.

background_sections.before: Reka made stop-motion films in Budapest for twelve years, moving puppets one frame at a time until they looked alive. She worked in a studio above a bakery in the eighth district. One of her short films won a prize at Annecy. She lived alone with a cat that hated every puppet she ever made.
background_sections.adjustment: It turned out that stop-motion was the best training for necromancy anyone's ever had. The first time she raised something, she said she knew exactly where she'd gone wrong with the elbow. She treats the dead the way she treated her puppets, with patience and a lot of small adjustments. She's sly, funny and very precise.
background_sections.forward: Reka wants to make something move that's never moved before, and she's careful not to say what. She's also looking for a good camera. She knows there isn't one on this world. She keeps looking anyway.
background_sections.now: She works on the Black Strand, in the black sand beneath the Dry Deep, raising crows out of whatever the beetles leave behind. The people there don't like what she does, but they appreciate how tidy she is about it. The little mannequin on her belt is the last thing she animated at home. It still has the wire in its arm.

recruits.look: Hungarian woman, 30, slim, glossy dark chestnut hair to her shoulders with a heavy fringe, pale skin, large dark-hazel eyes. Charcoal and bone-white necromancer robes with a high collar, a staff of bound bone, a small raised skeletal crow on her shoulder, a tiny wooden artist's mannequin on her belt.

recruits.name: Ramiro Quispe
recruits.backstory: Ramiro mined silver in Potosí, in the Cerro Rico, like his father and his grandfather, and he learned young that the mountain talks before it moves. He's steady, proud and quietly funny, and the Dark Iron of Onyxhollow took to him because he hears the rock the way they do. The earth answers him now, which he says is only fair after all the years he spent listening to it.
recruits.greeting: Listen, really listen. You can hear the rock settling. This town's built on good stone.

background_sections.before: Ramiro mined silver in the Cerro Rico above Potosi, in Bolivia, like his father and his grandfather before him. He worked twelve-hour shifts for a cooperative that never paid on time, and his wife ran a juice stall in the market. They had two daughters, and the elder wanted to be a geologist, so he was saving for her studies. He learned young that the mountain talks before it moves.
background_sections.adjustment: He landed underground, which was the one thing that made any sense. The first stone that lifted itself into his hand frightened him badly, and he's mostly used to it now. The earth answers him here, which he says is only fair after all the years he spent listening to it. His whole shift was in the mine with him that day.
background_sections.forward: Ramiro wants to know whether Potosi came through too, and whether anyone is still underneath it. He thinks about his shift every day. He's steady, proud and quietly funny. He'd like his daughter to know he's become a sort of geologist himself.
background_sections.now: He lives in Onyxhollow, in the mining quarter, and he spends most of his time listening to the rock. The Dark Iron took to him because he hears it the way they do. He's teaching the apprentices to timber a tunnel the way his father did, and they've stopped laughing at the method. His old carbide lamp hasn't had fuel in three years, and he keeps it polished anyway.

recruits.look: Bolivian man, 36, compact and powerful, black hair cropped short, warm brown skin, dark eyes. Primalist plate studded with raw stone in grey and ochre, a stone-headed stave, pebbles floating above his open hand, a dented brass carbide headlamp strapped to his belt.

recruits.name: Graham Ashworth
recruits.backstory: Nineteen years of night shifts at a hospice outside Preston taught Graham that a slow ending can be a kind one, if somebody pays attention. Affliction came to him easily, and that bothered him more than anything else here, until he worked out it's the same patience pointed the other way. He's gentle, tired and very good company.
recruits.greeting: Sit down a minute if you need to. Most people who come up this road do, and there's no shame in it.

background_sections.before: Graham grew up in Blackpool, where his dad drove the buses and his mum ran a cafe on the seafront. He trained as a nurse at twenty-two and spent the next nineteen years working nights at a hospice outside Preston. It was hard work, sitting with people in their last days and with the families waiting in the corridors, but he was good at it. His husband Tom taught music at a primary school and sang in the car whether Graham liked it or not, loudly and badly. They had a small house with a garden that Graham always meant to get round to and never did.
background_sections.adjustment: For his first year here Graham simply kept nursing, looking after anyone who needed it, living or dead. He spent his second year learning why the Forsaken didn't need him the way he expected them to. When he discovered he had a gift for affliction magic, the slow kind that wears an enemy down, it frightened him more than anything else about this world. He sat with it for months before he used it. In the end he decided it was the same patience he'd learned at the bedside, only pointed the other way.
background_sections.forward: Graham is looking for Tom, who he has no reason to believe came through, and every reason to hope. He reads the lists of the missing in every town he passes through, and he hasn't skipped one yet. He'd also like a garden at last, and there's a corner of ground at the Pale Watch he's had his eye on. If he finds Tom, he says, the first thing he'll do is plant something. If he doesn't, he'll plant it anyway.
background_sections.now: These days he's at the Pale Watch, where the plague creeps up close and slow, and he understands that kind of slowness better than most people. He looks after the sick and the frightened, and he sits with the ones who aren't going to get better. He still wears the nurse's watch Tom gave him, pinned upside down on his chest the way nurses do. It still runs, and he winds it every morning before he does anything else.

recruits.look: English man, 41, tall and fit, light brown hair going silver at the temples, light beard, blue-grey eyes. Dark violet and sickly green affliction robes with a long scarf, a staff with a cracked lantern, faint green motes, a nurse's fob watch pinned upside down on his chest.

recruits.name: Elie Khoury
recruits.backstory: Elie drew blood for a living at a clinic in Achrafieh, and he was the one the nervous patients asked for. He arrived here with a tourniquet in his pocket and found out that blood listens to him now. He heals with it, which most bloodmages think is a waste and he thinks is the only sensible use. He's calm, warm and careful, and very hard to rattle.
recruits.greeting: Give me your arm. I promise this is the least frightening thing you'll see in Khaz Varun.

background_sections.before: Elie drew blood at a clinic in Achrafieh, in Beirut, and he was the one the nervous patients always asked for. He spent his Sundays at his mother's table and kept an old motorbike running on spare parts and faith. For six years he'd been saving to go to medical school in Montpellier. He was close to having enough. He grew up beside the sea and swam in it almost every day of his life.
background_sections.adjustment: He arrived with a tourniquet in his pocket and soon found out that blood listened to him here. The first time he felt someone's blood move under his hand, he finished healing them before he let himself be frightened. Most bloodmages think healing with blood is a waste of the gift, and he thinks it's the only sensible use for it. He says the work is the same as it ever was, only without the needle.
background_sections.forward: Elie wants to teach other people to heal the way he does. The Ashclaim's healers keep asking him, and he keeps saying yes, even when he's tired. He'd also like to see the sea again, because he hasn't been near it in three years. He says Khaz Varun is the furthest from water he's ever lived, and he feels it every day.
background_sections.now: He works in the upper halls of Khaz Varun, patching up whoever comes out of the dark in worse shape than they went in. He's calm, warm and careful, and very hard to rattle. The blue needle cap clipped to his sleeve is from the last blood test he did at home. He's never taken it off.

recruits.look: Lebanese man, 33, slim and neat, black hair swept back, close trimmed beard, dark eyes. Crimson and black bloodmage robes over light mail, a short ritual knife and a slim staff, red threads of light at his fingers, a tourniquet band and a blue butterfly-needle cap clipped to his sleeve.

recruits.name: Bruno Teixeira
recruits.backstory: Bruno fought heavyweight in Curitiba, in small halls with loud crowds, and he was better at it than his record says. He joined the Scarlet Crusade in the first months because it was the only army winning, and he walked out of it beside Rory Callahan the night they burned the transplant camp. He's huge, cheerful and very hard to knock down, and he fights like the bell's about to go.
recruits.greeting: Rory says I smile too much for a templar. I tell him somebody in the Order has to.

background_sections.before: Bruno grew up in Curitiba, in the south of Brazil, where his mother, Dona Graca, raised him on her own after his father left. At fifteen he walked into a gym above a tyre shop and met Seu Valdir, the coach who made him a fighter. He fought heavyweight in small, noisy halls, and won eighteen of his twenty-three fights. He'll tell you he was better than his record says. His mother came to every fight and covered her eyes for all of them, and he always found her in the crowd before the bell.
background_sections.adjustment: He was wrapping his hands at the gym when the world changed, and he came round in the Plaguelands with a roll of hand-wrap in his pocket. In those first months he joined the Scarlet Crusade, because it was the only army winning and it wanted big men who could fight. They taught him the Light, and that's the part he kept. He walked out beside Rory Callahan the night the Crusade burned a camp of people from home, and he doesn't talk about that night unless Rory does first.
background_sections.forward: Bruno wants the Order to grow big enough that nobody ever has to choose between the Crusade and nothing again, the way he had to. He's teaching the Bulwark's recruits to fight with their hands, and he's delighted with every one of them. He still hasn't found his mother. Some nights he catches himself looking for her at the edge of the training yard, with her hands over her face.
background_sections.now: He lives in the Order's quarter of the Bulwark now, and he trains anyone who'll stand in front of him. He's huge, cheerful and very hard to knock down, and he fights as if the bell's about to go. Rory says he smiles too much for a templar, and Bruno says somebody in the Order has to. The black hand-wrap on his belt is from his last fight at home, which he won.

recruits.look: Brazilian man, 34, huge through the chest and shoulders, short dark brown hair, light olive skin, short dark beard, warm brown eyes. Grey steel templar plate with a white tabard bearing a pale flame, a two-handed warhammer with white holy fire, a roll of black fighter's hand-wrap tucked in his belt.

recruits.name: Joaquín Duarte
recruits.backstory: Joaquín taught history at a secondary school in Rosario until the Integration. In the Crusade they made him an interrogator, because he was patient and he listened, and he was good at it in a way he'll be sorry for until he dies. He left with Rory Callahan. Now he heals with the same hands, and he fights with them too, and he carries what he did there without asking anyone to carry it for him.
recruits.greeting: If you've got something heavy to put down, the Order's a good place to do it. I'd know.

background_sections.before: Joaquin taught history at a secondary school in Rosario, in Argentina, with a mate gourd on his desk and a novel he'd been writing for nine years in his drawer. He was good with the difficult kids, because he actually listened to them. He liked teaching fifteen-year-olds more than most people would believe. He thought he'd do it until he retired.
background_sections.adjustment: In his first months here he joined the Scarlet Crusade, and they made him an interrogator, because he was patient and he listened. He was good at it, in a way he'll be sorry for until the day he dies. He says he adjusted too well, and that's the whole problem. Rory Callahan found him in a cell in Hearthglen at four in the morning, sitting with a prisoner he'd been told to break, and the two of them walked out together.
background_sections.forward: Joaquin is writing down the name of everyone he ever questioned. He wants to find the ones who survived and apologise to their faces. He's found four so far, and two of them hit him. He says they were right to.
background_sections.now: He's at the Bulwark with the Order now, healing the wounded who come in from the Plaguelands. He heals with the same hands he used in that cell, and he fights with them too. He carries what he did without asking anyone to carry it for him. The mate gourd at his hip is the one from his classroom desk, and he still drinks from it every morning.

recruits.look: Argentine man, 38, tall and lean, dark hair a little long and swept back, close dark beard, dark eyes, a handsome haunted face. Grey mail over a white undercoat with a pale flame on the chest, hands wrapped for fist-fighting, sun-gold light at his knuckles, a worn leather mate gourd and silver bombilla at his hip.

recruits.name: Astrid Nyström
recruits.backstory: Astrid photographed the aurora above Kiruna for tourists and magazines, and spent most of her twenties lying in snow waiting for the sky to do something. She arrived here on a clear night with her camera round her neck, and the stars answered her within the week. She hunts by starlight in North Felwood now. She's calm and bright and very good at waiting for the right moment.
recruits.greeting: Clear nights are the best ones up here. The stars are wrong, but they're very bright.

background_sections.before: Astrid grew up in Lulea, in the north of Sweden, and at twenty-two she moved to Kiruna to photograph the aurora. She stayed twelve years, in a cabin with no road to it in winter and a camera worth more than her car. She took tourists out into the snow at night and sold her best shots to magazines, but mostly she lay in the snow and waited for the sky to do something. Her brother Erik lived in Stockholm and called every Sunday to ask if she was still alive. She always said barely, and he always laughed.
background_sections.adjustment: She was out on a clear night photographing the northern lights when everything changed, and she came round in Felwood with the camera still round her neck. It died within the week, and she found that harder to bear than almost anything else. The Sentinels at Talonbranch taught her to use a bow, and the stars taught her the rest. They answered her within days, as if they'd been waiting for someone to ask.
background_sections.forward: Astrid is mapping the new sky star by star, in a notebook the size of a brick. The stars here are wrong, but they're brighter than any she ever photographed, and she wants to know all of them. She'd like to find Erik and hear him ask if she's still alive. She knows it isn't likely, and she keeps the Sunday habit anyway.
background_sections.now: She hunts in North Felwood now, out near the Talonbranch camp, tracking whatever crawls out of the fel when the light gets low. She's calm and very good at waiting for the right moment, which is most of what her old job was. She still wears the lens cap from her dead camera on a cord round her neck. Every Sunday evening she stops what she's doing at the time Erik used to call.

recruits.look: Swedish woman, 32, slim and athletic, long platinum-blonde hair in a loose braid, pale skin, ice-blue eyes. Silver and midnight-blue sentinel leathers, a tall bow strung with faint starlight, star motes along the arrows, a small camera lens cap on a cord round her neck.

recruits.name: Luka Perić
recruits.backstory: Luka captained a car ferry between Split and the islands for fifteen years, and he knows the sea well enough to be properly afraid of it. The storm found him on the crossing, and it's been following him since. He calls it up now on the Tempest Shallows, carefully, the way he used to read the weather off the Adriatic. He's wry, weathered and the steadiest person in any room.
recruits.greeting: Have you ever watched a squall come in over open water? I have, many times, so stand behind me and you'll be fine.

background_sections.before: Luka captained a car ferry called the Marjan between Split and the Croatian islands for fifteen years, with a crew of eight. He knew the sea well enough to be properly afraid of it. His wife ran a little tavern on the island of Brac, and their son played water polo, badly. Luka never missed a single match.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke up on a beach with the ferry's brass whistle in his hand and no ferry anywhere. The storm found him on that crossing, and it's been following him ever since. The first storm he called up nearly drowned him, and he says that's how he knew it was his. Now he calls them carefully, the way he used to read the weather coming off the Adriatic.
background_sections.forward: Luka wants a boat of his own, small and sound, and he'd sail it home tomorrow if he knew which way home was. Until then he'll keep teaching the crews. He thinks about his son's matches more than he expected to. He'd give a lot to watch one more, even a bad one.
background_sections.now: He's on the Tempest Shallows now, near the landing, watching the sky. He's wry and weathered, and the steadiest person in any room. He's teaching the Ashclaim's boat crews to read the weather before it reads them. Every evening he blows the Marjan's whistle once, at the time the last ferry used to leave.

recruits.look: Croatian man, 39, tall and broad-shouldered, short dark hair with some grey, short beard, sea-blue eyes. Deep sea-green and storm-grey robes with a short cloak that drips water, a driftwood staff bound in silver, frost and spray at his feet, a brass ship's whistle on a lanyard.

recruits.name: Zofia Nowak
recruits.backstory: Zofia answered phones for an insurance company in Łódź, eight hours a day of people shouting at her about things she couldn't fix. The Cult of the Damned found her in the first winter and promised her that she'd never be powerless again, and for a while they kept the promise. Then she saw what it cost, and she walked out of Andorhal with what they'd taught her. She's guarded and determined, and nobody talks down to her twice.
recruits.greeting: I know what these robes look like. I tore their symbols off myself, so you can stop staring.

background_sections.before:
A call centre, a flat with her grandmother, and a night course in accounting she was two exams from finishing.

Her grandmother taught her to play cards and cheated every single time.
background_sections.adjustment:
She'd rather not talk about the first year, and she'll tell you that plainly.

She left Andorhal at night, alone, and she took three of the Cult's books with her.
background_sections.forward:
She wants every Cult house in the Plaguelands burned, and she knows where most of them are.

After that she'd like to finish the accounting course, and she's not joking.
background_sections.now:
In the north of the Western Plaguelands, near Andorhal, hunting the people who recruited her.

The headset clip pinned to her collar is from her desk at the call centre, and she wears it like a medal.

recruits.look: Polish woman, 29, slender, long dark-brown hair loose past her shoulders, pale skin, dark eyes, a serious face. Deep violet and black shadow robes with the Cult's symbols torn off and the stitches showing, a thin dark staff, shadow at her fingertips, a black plastic headset clip pinned to her collar.

recruits.name: Sherif Gamal
recruits.backstory: Sherif did pest control in Cairo, fumigating apartment blocks and restaurants and once, memorably, a museum storeroom. He's spent his whole working life very calm around things that sting, and the Royal Hive is full of them. He arrived with his fumigation rig on his back and found out venom listens to him here. He's unbothered, amused and the only person who walks into the hive without flinching.
recruits.greeting: Don't swat at them. Things that sting only get worse when you panic, and they can tell.

background_sections.before: Sherif did pest control in Cairo, fumigating apartment blocks, restaurants and once, memorably, a museum storeroom. It was a family business his father started in 1987, run out of a van with a fogging machine in the back. He spent his whole working life very calm around things that sting. He was engaged to a pharmacist called Mariam, and their wedding was set for the following spring.
background_sections.adjustment: He arrived with his fumigation rig still on his back and found that venom listens to him here. He says the bugs are bigger and otherwise it's the same job. He means it as a joke, and he also means it. He's unbothered and amused by almost everything, which unsettles people.
background_sections.forward: Sherif is studying every poison in the hive, because he believes a poison you understand is half an antidote. He's also looking for Mariam. He asks every healer he meets about her, because he knows she'd have ended up near the sick. He hasn't stopped asking, and he doesn't intend to.
background_sections.now: He works inside the Royal Hive, in the first chambers, cataloguing everything that lives there. He's the only person who walks into the hive without flinching. The brass nozzle hanging from his belt came off his old fogging rig. He still checks it for blockages out of habit.

recruits.look: Egyptian man, 35, medium build and very fit, short black hair, trimmed beard, dark eyes, a calm face. Dark green and sand venomancer robes with a hooded mantle, glass vials and spore pods on a bandolier, a staff with a coiled serpent, a brass fumigation nozzle hanging from his belt.

recruits.name: Santiago Ríos
recruits.backstory: Santiago tattooed in Medellín, in a shop in Laureles with a waiting list that ran for months. He arrived with the grip of his machine in his pocket, and runes started showing up in his work within the month. He engraves them into his blades now, and into his own arms, and they burn when he fights. He's confident, bright and a perfectionist about line work in a way that makes the Ashclaim's smiths nervous.
recruits.greeting: Every rune's a line you can't take back. Same as a tattoo, really, just a lot louder.

background_sections.before:
A shop with his cousin, three hundred clients' worth of designs in a folder, and a little brother he was putting through school.

His mother never approved of the tattoos and had a small one done anyway, by him.
background_sections.adjustment:
The first rune he cut glowed, and he spent a week trying to work out what he'd done right.

He worked it out, and his arms are proof.
background_sections.forward:
A rune nobody's ever cut before. He's filled three notebooks trying.

He's also looking for his brother, who was at school in Bogotá that day.
background_sections.now:
On the Ashen Reach, near the works, cutting runes into anything that'll hold still.

The tattoo machine grip on his hip is from his station at the shop, and he still cleans it every night.

recruits.look: Colombian man, 28, lean and athletic, black hair in a short fade with a longer top, light stubble, dark eyes, glowing rune tattoos down both forearms. Charcoal and electric-blue battle-wraps, a runed blade in each hand, a black and steel tattoo machine grip on a cord at his hip.

recruits.name: Emiliano Vargas
recruits.backstory: At the traffic lights in Oaxaca, Emiliano breathed fire for coins from car windows, two minutes a red light. He was good at it and very good at talking, and he arrived with a bottle of lamp oil on his belt. The fire here took to him at once. Now it comes out of him the colour of a dragon's breath, and he's cocky about it, and he's earned some of that.
recruits.greeting: Want to see a trick? I used to do this for coins at a red light, and now I do it for the Ashclaim.

background_sections.before: Emiliano breathed fire at the traffic lights in Oaxaca, two minutes every red light, for coins handed out of car windows. He worked a corner near the zocalo for eleven years and never burned himself once, and he'll show you his hands to prove it. He was the oldest of five, with four younger sisters he helped support. He dreamed of a circus that would take him on one day. He was very good at the fire and even better at the talking.
background_sections.adjustment: He arrived with a bottle of lamp oil on his belt, and the fire here took to him at once. Now it comes out of him the colour of a dragon's breath, and he's cocky about it, and he's earned some of that. He says the Integration finally gave him the stage he always wanted, and he only half means it. The Ashclaim hired him the day he lit their forge from across the yard.
background_sections.forward: Emiliano wants to put on a real show, in a real tent, for an audience that's paid to get in. He's already worked out the order of the acts. He also sends money home on every ship that leaves Cinderwharf, in case one of them somehow finds his sisters. He knows it won't, and he does it anyway.
background_sections.now: He lives in Cinderwharf, near the forges, and he shows off to anyone who'll stand still long enough to watch. The Ashclaim's smiths pretend to be annoyed by him and secretly look forward to it. He still carries the same bottle of lamp oil he had at home, and the label's nearly worn away. He won't fill it, and he won't throw it away.

recruits.look: Mexican man, 29, slim and wiry, black hair a little wild, thin moustache, dark eyes, a cocky grin. Scarlet and gold pyromancer robes with dragon-scale trim and a draconic collar, a slim rod, a curl of flame at his lips, a plastic bottle of lamp oil with a faded label on his belt.

recruits.name: Isla Fraser
recruits.backstory: Isla stalked deer in the Highlands for the estates and shot biathlon for Scotland, and she's the stillest person you'll ever meet with a weapon in her hands. She stayed well clear of the Crusade. She joined the Order of the Pale Flame after Rory Callahan walked out of it, because she'd watched the Order do the work cleanly. She's sharp, level and quietly kind once the shooting stops.
recruits.greeting: I don't miss, and I'd rather not have to prove it today. Is there something you need?

background_sections.before: Isla grew up in a cottage above Glen Affric, in the Scottish Highlands, and stalked deer for the estates from the age of fourteen. She also shot biathlon for Scotland, skiing and shooting, and she's the stillest person you'll ever meet with a weapon in her hands. The month before the Integration she'd qualified for the World Cup. Her dad had already booked the time off work to come and watch her.
background_sections.adjustment: She spent her first year alone, hunting whatever needed hunting in the Plaguelands. She stayed well clear of the Scarlet Crusade, because she didn't like what she saw of it. Then she met the Order of the Pale Flame, which Rory Callahan founded after he walked out of the Crusade. They were the first people she'd met here who didn't waste a shot, so she joined them.
background_sections.forward: Isla wants Stratholme cleared, properly, and she means to be there when it happens. She'd also like to hear her dad laugh again. She keeps that one to herself. On quiet nights she still checks the weather the way she did before a race.
background_sections.now: She's at Light's Hope Chapel with the Order's camp now, keeping watch over the eastern road. She's sharp and level, and quietly kind once the shooting stops. The steel buckle on her crossbow strap came off her old biathlon rifle sling. She's never once thought about replacing it.

recruits.look: Scottish woman, 31, athletic and strong, long red hair in a thick braid, pale freckled skin, green eyes. A grey storm-coat over leathers with a white pale-flame pin, a heavy crossbow carried low, bolts at her hip, a worn steel biathlon rifle-sling buckle on her strap.

recruits.name: Dale Brekke
recruits.backstory: Dale farmed wheat outside Minot, North Dakota, on land his family had worked for four generations. He's big, slow-spoken and very hard to hurry, and he knows how to bring a harvest in before the weather turns. The scythe came naturally. He walks the plagued fields of the east now with it, and he says he's doing what he always did, which is clearing ground so something better can grow.
recruits.greeting: Bad ground out here, but it's ground. You'd be surprised what comes back if you give it time.

background_sections.before: Dale farmed wheat outside Minot, North Dakota, on two thousand acres his family had worked for four generations. He'd paid off the combine the spring before everything changed, and he was prouder of that than he let on. His wife ran the county co-op and knew everybody's business for fifty miles. Their kids had grown up and moved to Fargo and Denver, and they called every Sunday after church. Dale's whole life was getting a harvest in before the weather turned.
background_sections.adjustment: He took his time settling in, the way he takes his time with everything. The scythe came naturally to him, because he'd used one on the field edges since he was a boy. The first time he swung it at something dead, he said it felt like the last pass of a long harvest. After that he stopped worrying about what he'd become and got on with the work.
background_sections.forward: Dale wants to plant the Eastern Plaguelands one day, properly, with wheat that comes up clean. He tests the soil from every field he crosses and writes the results on the backs of old seed packets. Most of the readings are bad, but a few of them are getting better. He'd like his kids to see the first harvest, wherever they are.
background_sections.now: He's out in the Eastern Plaguelands now, working the blighted fields one row at a time. He says he's doing what he always did, which is clearing ground so something better can grow. He's big and slow-spoken and very hard to hurry. When the day's work is done, he puts on the seed-company cap he wore on the combine, which he keeps tucked in his belt.

recruits.look: American man, 44, big and broad, sandy-brown hair cut short, short greying beard, blue eyes, a rugged sun-creased face. Dark brown and iron reaper plate, plain and practical, a huge two-handed scythe carried low, a seed-company cap folded into his belt.

recruits.name: Mohammed Saleh
recruits.backstory: Mohammed and his sister Layla ran a guesthouse in Aqaba, on the Red Sea, full of divers who came for the coral. He's warm, chatty and remembers every guest's name and how they take their tea. When they came through, he took the first job going, keeping the inn at Talrendis Landing, and then the dreams started: the same white street running into the sea, every night, with the queen's court walking it. Here the dreams turned into something he can use, and now he sees a little way along time, backward and forward.
recruits.greeting: Sit down, you look tired. Layla keeps the inn now, and I keep the dreams. Lately the dreams are the busier job.

background_sections.before: Mohammed and his sister Layla ran a guesthouse in Aqaba, on the Red Sea, with twelve rooms over a dive shop and a rooftop where the guests ate breakfast looking across the water. It was always full of divers who'd come for the coral. Layla did the books, because he was hopeless at them. He made the tea himself every morning, remembered every guest's name and how they took it, and never let anyone leave without a second glass.
background_sections.adjustment: When he and Layla came through, he took the first job going, keeping the inn at Talrendis Landing, and kept doing what he knew, which was feeding people and letting them rest. That held him together. Then the dreams started, the same white street running into the sea every night. They frightened him until Farseer Thrag told him they were true. After that they mostly made him curious.
background_sections.forward: Mohammed wants to walk the street from his dreams while he's awake, just once, to see if it looks the way it does at night. Layla would rather he stopped dreaming and helped with the laundry. He says he can do both. So far the laundry is losing.
background_sections.now: Layla runs the inn at Talrendis Landing now, and Mohammed sits by the door with a glass of tea going cold beside him. The dreams turned into something he can use, and he can see a little way along time, backwards and forwards. He wears the guesthouse's brass front door key on a cord round his neck. In his head, he still locks up every night.

recruits.look: Jordanian man, 41, medium build, warm brown skin, short dark curly hair going grey at the temples, a neat short beard, kind dark eyes with laugh lines. Deep teal and sand chronomancer robes with brass trim and a small hourglass at the belt, a staff with a glass orb full of slow-turning sand, a brass key on a cord round his neck.

recruits.name: Lúcia Ferreira
recruits.backstory: Lúcia ran a salon in Goiânia with two chairs, a radio that only got one station and a queue on Saturdays. Her grandmother raised her on rosaries and saints' days, and Lúcia still prays the way she was taught, out loud and with her whole heart. She's warm, chatty and a shameless gossip who never repeats a word said in her chair. Here the sun answers when she asks, which surprised her a lot less than it surprised the priests.
recruits.greeting: Sit down, sit down, you've got half the Barrens in your hair. I'll fix it while you tell me everything.

background_sections.before: Lucia ran a salon in Goiania, in Brazil, with two chairs, pink tiles, a radio that only got one station and a queue every Saturday. She had a cat called Dona Flor, and her mother phoned every day at noon. Her grandmother raised her on rosaries and saints' days, and lit a candle every Sunday for everybody on their street, by name. Lucia kept the list for her. She was a shameless gossip who never repeated a word said in her chair.
background_sections.adjustment: She landed with her scissors in her apron pocket, and the first thing she did on this world was cut a grunt's hair. He tipped her a copper. She started praying at the Crossroads because she didn't know what else to do, out loud and with her whole heart, the way her grandmother taught her. The light came down on the second day, which surprised her a lot less than it surprised the priests.
background_sections.forward: Lucia wants a proper salon with a door that shuts and a mirror that isn't a bucket of water. She'd also like a church, any church at all, where someone will sing with her. She still keeps her grandmother's list. She's added a few names from this world to the bottom of it.
background_sections.now: She works at the Crossroads, by the inn, with a stool, a bowl of water and a queue of caravan guards. She charges a copper and a blessing for a haircut. Most of them pay the copper and pretend not to want the blessing. She gives it to them anyway, and they always come back.

recruits.look: Brazilian woman, 33, curvy, long dark-brown curly hair, warm golden-brown skin, large dark eyes. White and sun-gold cleric robes with a gold sun disc on the chest, a slim golden sceptre, hairdresser's scissors in a holster on her belt, a silver saint's medal on a chain.

recruits.name: Cristóbal Muñoz
recruits.backstory: Cristóbal was a wildfire brigadista in Valparaíso, and in 2024 he spent four days on the hills above his mother's house while the city burned. The house was still standing when he came down. He's brave, loud and reckless with himself but never with anybody else, and he calls everyone hermano within a minute of meeting them. Hellfire found him, which he says is a joke at his expense, and he's decided to laugh at it.
recruits.greeting: Hermano, you smell like smoke, which is good. It means you've been somewhere interesting.

background_sections.before: Cristobal was a wildfire fighter in Valparaiso, in Chile. In 2024 he spent four days on the hills above his mother's house while the city burned below him, and when he finally came down, the house was still standing. He worked out of a brigade station in the hills and rode a motorbike that broke down every week. His mother, Ines, sent him off to every shift with empanadas. He danced the cueca at every fiesta and was very bad at it, which he says was the point.
background_sections.adjustment: On his first day here he walked out of a grass fire, and he was the only one who did. A month later he discovered that hellfire answered him, which he says is a joke at his expense, and he's decided to laugh at it. The fire inside him frightened him for weeks. Then he started using it to light other people's camps, and that made it feel like his again.
background_sections.forward: Cristobal wants every town in the Barrens to have a fire brigade of its own, and he's training the first one now. He'd also like his mother to know he's alive. He writes her a letter every week, with nowhere to send it, and he keeps every one. There are more than a hundred and fifty of them now, tied up with string.
background_sections.now: He's at Camp Taurajo now, drilling a dozen young tauren on how to cut a firebreak. When the grass goes up in the dry season, he's the one Taurajo sends for. He's loud and brave and reckless with himself, but never with anyone else. He calls everyone hermano within a minute of meeting them.

recruits.look: Chilean man, 35, athletic and broad-shouldered, thick black hair pushed back, a short dark beard, warm brown skin, dark eyes, soot on his face. Dark crimson and black knightly plate with orange hellfire in the seams, a two-handed flamberge, a yellow brigadista's helmet clipped to his belt.

recruits.name: Iker Etxeberria
recruits.backstory: Iker taught PE and coached pelota in Lekeitio, a Basque fishing town, at a school with a fronton wall older than the church. He's never met anyone he couldn't shout into running one more lap, and he's never been tired in his life. He's loud, upbeat and competitive about absolutely everything. Here the shouting turned into something real, and when Iker tells a fighter they can keep going, they really can.
recruits.greeting: Up, up, up, come on! You can rest when you're dead, and you don't look dead to me.

background_sections.before: Iker taught PE and coached pelota in Lekeitio, a Basque fishing town, at a school of ninety children with a fronton wall older than the church. He rode an old bicycle everywhere, and his mother made the best burnt cheesecake in the province. He lived above the bakery with Unai, a fisherman, for six years. Unai left at four every morning and came home at noon, and Iker always had the coffee ready. He'd never been tired a day in his life, or so he claimed.
background_sections.adjustment: He landed in Arathi in the rain and had started a running club for the farmhands within a week. The first time his voice actually healed somebody, he didn't even notice. He just assumed they'd been lazy before. Here his shouting turned into something real, and when Iker tells a fighter they can keep going, they really can.
background_sections.forward: Iker wants a fronton wall in Arathi and somebody here who can play pelota properly. He keeps a sheet of paper in his pocket with ninety names on it. The whole school was in session that day, and he doesn't know where any of the children ended up. He thinks about Unai every morning, at about the time the coffee would have been ready.
background_sections.now: He's in Arathi West with a whistle round his neck and a line of tired farmhands jogging behind him. They complain about him all day long, and they've never been fitter in their lives. He's loud, upbeat and competitive about absolutely everything. He's never met anyone he couldn't shout into one more lap.

recruits.look: Basque man, 33, strong and compact, dark brown hair short at the sides, clean-shaven, a strong nose and jaw, brown eyes. Bright steel guardian half-plate over a red and white padded coat, a round shield and a short sword, a coach's silver whistle on a red cord.

recruits.name: Héctor Salinas
recruits.backstory: Héctor wrestled lucha libre in Mexico City for fifteen years as El Relámpago de Plata, the Silver Lightning, and nobody outside his family ever saw his face. He's a showman with a huge laugh, superstitious about everything and much smarter than he lets anyone see. The trolls of Stranglethorn told him a mask is a spirit's face, and he said he'd known that his whole life. Now the spirits wear his, and the crowds at the arena love him.
recruits.greeting: Ah, a fan! Don't be shy, everybody wants to meet El Relampago de Plata, even here.

background_sections.before: Hector wrestled lucha libre in Mexico City for fifteen years as El Relampago de Plata, the Silver Lightning, and nobody outside his family ever saw his face. He fought at Arena Mexico on Friday nights and trained at a gym in Tepito. His wife sewed every mask he ever wore, and their two boys wanted to be luchadores just like him. He retired a year before the Integration with a bad knee and a lot of good stories.
background_sections.adjustment: He arrived with his mask in his bag, and the first troll who saw it bowed to him. The trolls of Stranglethorn told him a mask is a spirit's face, and he said he'd known that his whole life. A witch doctor at Grom'gol took him in, and he learned shadow and spirit the same way he'd learned to fall, by doing it a thousand times. Now the spirits wear his mask, and the crowds love him for it.
background_sections.forward: Hector wants to put on a real show at the arena, with rules, a ring and a crowd that cheers instead of waiting for blood. He's already talking to the arena's owners about it. One day he'd like to see his mask on his boys' faces. He's afraid he never will, and he doesn't say so.
background_sections.now: He spends his days at the Gurubashi Arena in Stranglethorn, signing autographs for goblins who can't read and posing for trolls. He's a showman with a huge laugh, superstitious about everything and much smarter than he lets anyone see. He never takes the mask off his belt. He says a luchador who loses his mask loses his name, and he isn't taking any chances.

recruits.look: Mexican man, 37, broad and powerful, short black hair and a sharp beard line, warm brown skin, dark eyes. Dark violet and bone witch-doctor robes with feathers and charms, a gnarled staff topped with a carved mask, a black luchador mask with silver flame trim on his belt.

recruits.name: Tobias Keller
recruits.backstory: Tobias worked on the Cologne Cathedral works crew, the team that's been repairing the cathedral for seven hundred years and will never finish. He replaced stones carved by men who died in the middle ages, and he loved it. He's patient, methodical and quietly devout, and he says very little, but all of it's true. The Light came to him the way good mortar sets, slowly, and it holds.
recruits.greeting: Mind the scaffold. That wall's coming along, but I'd rather you didn't lean on it yet.

background_sections.before:
A flat in the Südstadt, a crew of twelve who ate lunch together on the roof and a choir he sang bass in.

He carved a little face into every stone he ever replaced, somewhere nobody would ever look.
background_sections.adjustment:
He landed in the Plaguelands, which was very bad luck. The Argent Dawn took him in because he could fix a wall, and he's been fixing their walls since.

He found the Light on a scaffold, and he still prays best with a trowel in his hand.
background_sections.forward:
For Light's Hope to stand a thousand years, and to be the one who made it.

He'd also like to sing in a choir again. He's started one, and it has three people in it.
background_sections.now:
At Light's Hope Chapel, on the scaffold by the chapel wall, repointing mortar.

There's a little carved face on one of the new stones already. He won't say which one.

recruits.look: German man, 39, tall and broad, short light-brown hair, a neat short beard, grey-blue eyes. Polished silver paladin plate with a white tabard and a golden sun, a large kite shield and a mace, a stonemason's leather apron rolled at his waist with a chisel and mallet.

recruits.name: Camila Ortega
recruits.backstory: Camila worked in a lab in Durango, where the scorpions come into houses every summer, milking them for the venom that makes antivenom. She's done it ten thousand times, with tweezers and a steady hand. She's still, watchful and dryly funny, with nerves of steel, and she's fond of the things everyone else is scared of. Tanaris is full of scorpids, and she thinks it's the best place she's ever been.
recruits.greeting: Stand still, please. There's a scorpid under your boot, and it's having a worse day than you.

background_sections.before: Camila worked in a laboratory in Durango, where scorpions come into people's houses every summer. Her job was milking them for the venom used to make antivenom, and she'd done it ten thousand times with tweezers and a steady hand. She lived in a flat above a bakery, and her little sister Daniela called her every night to complain about boys. Once she saved a boy's life at the hospital next door, with antivenom she'd made that same week. She still thinks about him.
background_sections.adjustment: The first time a venomancer showed her what poison could do here, she asked for the dose, the timing and the antidote, in that order. The venomancers had never met anyone who wanted the antidote first, and they liked her immediately. She found that she was very good at waiting for something to move, and on this world that's most of the job. Nothing about the desert frightened her, and that frightened the people around her a little.
background_sections.forward: Camila wants an antivenom for every sting in Tanaris, and she's already made six of them. She keeps careful notes on each one, because she knows someone will need them after she's gone. She'd also like news of Daniela, and what she's doing now. She hopes it's something to do with boys.
background_sections.now: She lives in Northern Tanaris now, and you'll usually find her sitting very still on a rock, watching the sand. Tanaris is full of scorpids, and she thinks it's the best place she's ever been. There's always one on her shoulder. It's never the same one, and it never stings her.

recruits.look: Mexican woman, 29, slim and lithe, long wavy dark-brown hair tied back, golden-tan skin, sharp dark eyes. Close-fitting dark green and black stalker leathers with a short hooded mantle, two curved daggers dripping green venom, an amber scorpion on her shoulder, lab safety glasses pushed up into her hair.

recruits.name: Sebastián Cruz
recruits.backstory: Sebastián ran the grill at a steakhouse in Palermo, in Buenos Aires, for twelve years, the one his grandmother ran before him. He knows meat, blood and fire better than anyone, and he's cheerful about all three. He's sociable, a born host and completely unbothered by gore, and he'll feed anybody who sits down. He landed in Tirisfal, among the Forsaken, and they find his blood magic deeply unsettling, mostly because he's so happy about it.
recruits.greeting: You look hungry, my friend. I've got something on the coals, and I promise it isn't anyone you know.

background_sections.before:
A parrilla with forty tables, a football club he'd die for and a grandmother who ran the kitchen before him.

Every Sunday he cooked asado for his whole family, twenty people, and he didn't sit down at his own table once. He's never noticed.
background_sections.adjustment:
The Forsaken don't eat much, which was the hardest thing he's ever had to accept.

Blood magic came easy, because he's been reading blood on a grill his whole life. He knows when it's ready.
background_sections.forward:
A grill in Brill that the living and the dead will both come to.

He's working on a recipe the Forsaken can actually taste, and he thinks he's close.
background_sections.now:
In Western Tirisfal, by a fire pit he dug himself, with a grill and a very worried farmer.

He waves at every passing Forsaken, and some of them have started waving back.

recruits.look: Argentine man, 34, lean and tall, dark brown hair swept back, a short neat beard, light olive skin, brown eyes. Deep crimson and black bloodmage robes with a leather apron over them, a slim rod with a blood-red crystal, a big carving knife in a sheath with a white cloth round the handle.

recruits.name: Enzo Marchetti
recruits.backstory: Enzo fenced sabre for Naples from the age of eight and came fourth at the Olympic trials, twice. Fourth is the worst place there is. He's proud, intense and charming when he wants to be, and he's honest with himself about what he traded. The Scarlets wanted his blade and he turned them down, because he'd seen what they do. A darker god offered more, and now he's the best swordsman he's ever met, and he's still deciding if it was worth it.
recruits.greeting: You're watching my feet, and that's good, because that's where everybody should look. Most people watch the blade.

background_sections.before: Enzo fenced sabre for Naples from the age of eight and came fourth at the Olympic trials twice, and he'll tell you fourth is the worst place there is. He trained at a salle in the Spanish Quarter. His mother came to every bout and shouted at the referees, and he rode a scooter that was always parked illegally. On Saturdays he coached the little ones, and he was far kinder to them than he ever was to himself.
background_sections.adjustment: He landed with nothing but his fencing glove in his kit bag. The Scarlet Crusade found him first and wanted his blade, and then he saw what they did to people and walked away. Later, a darker voice offered him more, and it didn't lie to him about the price. He respects it for that. Now he's the best swordsman he's ever met.
background_sections.forward: Enzo wants to beat the best blade on this world, fairly, in front of witnesses. After that he'd like to know whether he could have done it without the voice. He's afraid he already knows the answer. He still hasn't decided whether the trade was worth it.
background_sections.now: He waits on the grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, outside the walls, watching the Scarlets drill and finding the holes in their technique. He's proud and intense, and charming when he wants to be, and honest with himself about what he traded. His white fencing glove is tucked in his belt. He doesn't wear it any more, and he won't throw it away.

recruits.look: Italian man, 34, slim and athletic, short black curly hair, clean-shaven with a sharp jaw, dark eyes. Black and dark violet cultist battle-robes over close mail, a long single-edged curved blade with purple shadow along it, a white fencing glove tucked into his belt.

recruits.name: Taras Kovalenko
recruits.backstory: Taras took tourists into the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone for nine years. He walked them through Pripyat, past the school and the swimming pool, and every tour ended under the yellow Ferris wheel that had stood still since 1986. He's dry, morbid and very gentle with animals, and he crossed over with Kashtan, a Zone stray he'd been feeding at the checkpoint for years. When the wheel turned up in Deadwind, he was the first to volunteer, because he's the one person on this world who knows it by heart.
recruits.greeting: Stay on the path, please, and don't touch anything that glows. I've said that to a lot of tourists, and I've never meant it more.

background_sections.before:
A flat in Kyiv with a balcony full of his mother's tomatoes, and a minibus that smelled of instant coffee.

He knew every dog at every checkpoint by name, and they all knew his pockets had sausage in them.
background_sections.adjustment:
Kashtan settled in faster than he did. The dog found the first hunting trail in a week, and Taras followed him onto a witch hunter's road.

He told himself the wheel was a coincidence for about a day, and then he stopped telling himself that.
background_sections.forward:
To stand under the wheel one more time and work out why it came here when nothing else did.

Then he'd like to find a quiet village, a lot of dogs and nothing radioactive at all.
background_sections.now:
At the liquidators' camp in Deadwind Pass, checking everyone through the wash troughs at the gate.

He counts heads when people go out and counts them again when they come back. Kashtan won't set a paw where the ground's gone bad, and Taras has learned not to either.

recruits.look: Ukrainian man, 38, tall and lean, dark-blond hair cut short, light stubble, grey-blue eyes. A long dark grey witch-hunter coat over leathers, a wide-brimmed hat, a short crossbow and a hunting spear, a brown shepherd-mix stray at his heel, a yellow and black dosimeter badge on his collar.

recruits.name: Wes Dahlberg
recruits.backstory: Wes spent twenty years on the Hanford tank farms in Washington, cleaning up waste that'll outlive everybody who ever made it. He did it in a suit, by the procedure, with a partner, every single day. He's slow to speak and impossible to rattle, and he's the kind of man who reads the whole manual before he touches anything. Standing in front of something bad so other people don't have to is the only job he's ever wanted, so Deadwind suits him fine.
recruits.greeting: Suit check before you go past the fence. I don't care who you are, I check everybody.

background_sections.before:
A house in Richland with a boat in the driveway that he took out twice a year, and two daughters in college.

He coached his younger girl's softball team for six seasons and didn't raise his voice in all that time.
background_sections.adjustment:
The fighting came easy, because the shield works like the procedure does. You hold it, you don't panic and you don't step out of line.

The hard part was never knowing if his girls were all right, and he still doesn't know.
background_sections.forward:
The fallout boxed up, mapped and labelled, the way it should've been done at Hanford.

After that, a boat again. There's a lake in Ashenvale he's had his eye on.
background_sections.now:
At the liquidators' camp in Deadwind Pass, at the quarantine fence, checking suits.

The camp's mule follows him everywhere. He says he doesn't know why, and he feeds it apples.

recruits.look: American man, 46, very big and broad, sandy-brown hair cut short, a short greying beard, blue eyes. Heavy, scratched dull-steel plate, a big rectangular tower shield and a broad sword, a faded yellow hazmat hood rolled up through his belt.

recruits.name: Mariana Treviño
recruits.backstory: Mariana was a radiation therapist at a cancer centre in Monterrey. She spent her days lining up beams to the millimetre, so the radiation hit the tumour and nothing else. She's calm, precise and kind, with a gallows humour she only lets other medics see. She heals with the Light now, and she aims it the same way. When the liquidators asked for someone who wasn't afraid of the word radiation, she packed that night.
recruits.greeting: Come in and sit on the cot. I'll tell you what I'm doing before I do it, so nothing's a surprise.

background_sections.before: Mariana was a radiation therapist at a cancer centre in Monterrey for ten years. She spent her days lining up beams to the millimetre, so the radiation hit the tumour and nothing else. She remembered every patient's birthday, and she rang a little bell for each of them on their last day of treatment. She ran with a club that met at five every morning, and her brother ran a taco stand by the stadium.
background_sections.adjustment: She found the Light the same way she'd always found the right dose, carefully and with a lot of notes. The priests in Orgrimmar told her she prayed like an accountant, and she took it as a compliment. She heals with the Light now, and she aims it exactly the way she aimed the beams. When the liquidators asked for someone who wasn't afraid of the word radiation, she packed that same night.
background_sections.forward: Mariana is keeping a record of everything the fallout does to a body, so whoever comes after her has something to work from. It's the only record of its kind. One day she'd like to run again, somewhere that doesn't glow. She still has the little bell, and she rings it when someone walks out of her infirmary cured.
background_sections.now: She runs the infirmary at the liquidators' camp, Ariden's Watch, in Deadwind Pass, working by lamplight with a stack of notebooks. The Forsaken apothecaries bring her their worst cases, and they've stopped arguing with her charts. She's calm, precise and kind. She has a gallows humour she only lets other medics see.

recruits.look: Mexican woman, 31, slim, glossy black hair in a high ponytail, light olive-tan skin, warm dark-brown eyes. White and pale gold priest robes with a long open overcoat, a short staff with a glowing white crystal, a hospital ID badge on a teal lanyard.

recruits.name: Neil Hartley
recruits.backstory: Neil spent twenty years decommissioning the old buildings at Sellafield, on the Cumbrian coast, taking apart things that were never meant to be taken apart. He's dry, unflappable and pedantic about safety, and he makes truly awful jokes about half-lives. Fel fire came to him like a bad habit, and he treats it like everything else that's dangerous, with a lot of respect and a written plan. He's the calmest man in Deadwind, and he'd like everyone else to calm down as well.
recruits.greeting: Hard hat's optional, but I'd stand behind me if I were you. The green bit doesn't care whose side you're on.

background_sections.before: Neil spent twenty years decommissioning the old buildings at Sellafield, on the Cumbrian coast, taking apart things that were never meant to be taken apart. He lived in a terraced house in Whitehaven, held a season ticket for the rugby league, and was married to a woman who did the crossword in pen. He walked the fells every Sunday and kept a list of every summit he'd climbed, in order. He makes truly awful jokes about half-lives.
background_sections.adjustment: The first time fel fire came out of his hands, he put it out, filled in a report, and then tried again. The warlocks found him maddening, because he wanted to know the dose of everything. Fel came to him like a bad habit, and he treats it like everything else that's dangerous, with a lot of respect and a written plan. He's dry, unflappable and pedantic about safety.
background_sections.forward: Neil wants to know what the fallout is actually made of, because he doesn't think anyone has asked the right questions yet. He's keeping careful records in case someone else has to finish the work. He'd also like a proper cup of tea. He's given up on that one.
background_sections.now: He works at the liquidators' camp in Deadwind Pass, mostly at the sample racks, labelling jars. He's put up a sign by the pyre telling people how long it's safe to stand near it. Nobody reads it, and he keeps updating it anyway. He's the calmest man in Deadwind, and he'd like everyone else to calm down as well.

recruits.look: English man, 44, tall and fit, grey hair with some dark left in it, a neat short beard, green eyes. Black and iron felsworn robes over light plate with green fel runes, a staff with a caged green flame, a white hard hat with a reflective stripe hanging from his belt.

recruits.name: Valentina Soto
recruits.backstory: Valentina took tourists out into the Atacama desert at night to look at the stars, in Spanish, English and Portuguese. She always found the Southern Cross first and always cried a little when someone saw the Milky Way for the first time. She's bright, curious and a born teacher who gets lost in the sky. Here the stars answer her, and the druids of Moonglade have been teaching her what they mean.
recruits.greeting: Look up at it, really look. I've never seen anything like the sky over this lake, and I've seen a lot of sky.

background_sections.before:
A hostel in San Pedro de Atacama with a telescope on the roof and four dogs that belonged to nobody.

She was studying for an astronomy degree by correspondence, and she was two courses short.
background_sections.adjustment:
The first night she looked up, she didn't recognise a single star. She sat down and cried, and then she started drawing new charts.

By the end of the month the stars were answering her, and she's been fighting by their light since.
background_sections.forward:
She wants to finish her chart of this world's sky, all of it, and name the constellations properly.

She also wants to know if Earth's sun is up there somewhere, and she's afraid of the answer.
background_sections.now:
In Moonglade, out by the lake, where she can see the most sky.

She carries a little red torch so she doesn't ruin her night eyes, and she makes visitors use it too.

recruits.look: Chilean woman, 28, athletic and slim, long straight black hair over one shoulder, warm tan skin, dark almond eyes. Silver and night-blue warden armour, a long glaive with a crescent blade edged in starlight, a small red-lens torch on a cord round her neck.

recruits.name: Faris Al-Tamimi
recruits.backstory: Faris grew dates on his family's land along the Shatt al-Arab outside Basra, where the Tigris and the Euphrates meet. His grandfather taught him that you look after the water first and the palms look after themselves. He's gentle, patient and a very good listener, and he misses home with his whole body. The water spirits here took to him at once, and Moonglade's lake is the first water since home that he trusts.
recruits.greeting: Peace be with you. Sit by the water for a while, it's good water. I can tell.

background_sections.before: Faris grew dates on his family's land along the Shatt al-Arab outside Basra, where the Tigris and the Euphrates meet. There were ninety palms, a house with a courtyard and a fig tree, and a big family that ate together every Friday. His grandfather taught him that you look after the water first and the palms look after themselves. He used to take his nephews out on the river in a flat boat and teach them the name of every bird they saw.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke in dry country, and for weeks he couldn't sleep without the sound of water. In the end a shaman found him sitting by a spring, talking to it, and told him the spring was talking back. The water spirits took to him at once after that. He's gentle and patient and a very good listener, and he misses home with his whole body.
background_sections.forward: Faris wants to plant something here that will still be standing in a hundred years. He's been trying to grow a date palm from the stone of the last date he had in his pocket when he arrived. So far it hasn't sprouted, but he waters it every morning. He's told it about the river at home.
background_sections.now: He lives in Moonglade now, by the lake, looking after the water and the people who come to it. It's the first water since home that he truly trusts. He wears his grandfather's prayer beads round his wrist and turns them when he's thinking. He greets everyone with peace, and he means it.

recruits.look: Iraqi man, 36, medium build and very fit, short black wavy hair, a close-trimmed beard, warm brown skin, dark eyes. River-blue and palm-green shaman mail and leathers, a wooden totem staff carved with fish and reeds, amber prayer beads round his wrist.

recruits.name: Álvaro Ruiz
recruits.backstory: Álvaro kept bees in the hills above Cartagena for twenty years, eighty hives on his uncle's land and honey sold off the back of a pickup on the coast road. He's been stung more times than he can count, and he's never once panicked about it. He came through on the ground like everyone else and climbed the tree with the first troll crews. On Rootwater Isle the swarms and the spiders leave him alone, and the venomancers took one look at that and taught him the rest.
recruits.greeting: Stand still if something lands on you, that's the whole trick. Nothing on this island has stung me yet, and I've given it every chance.

background_sections.before: Alvaro kept bees for twenty years in the hills above Cartagena, eighty hives along the fence of his uncle's coffee farm. His wife Marisela sold the honey off the back of a pickup truck on the coast road, and she sold it far better than he ever kept it. The truck had no second gear and he never got round to fixing it. Every morning he told the bees the news, because his grandfather had taught him that bees leave if you don't. Marisela laughed at him for it, and then she always asked what he'd told them.
background_sections.adjustment: He was standing among the hives at dawn with the smoker in his hand when he came through. The first wasp he met on this world was the size of his hand, and it landed on his arm, walked around for a while and flew off. The troll who saw it happen didn't speak to him for a day. He climbed the World Tree with the first troll crews, and the venomancers took one look at how the swarms ignored him and taught him everything they knew.
background_sections.forward: Alvaro wants to find a hive on this world that makes real honey, and keep it the way he kept his eighty. He'd also like to get word home somehow, the way he gave the bees their news every morning. He knows that isn't possible, and he still thinks about it every day. His uncle died the week before he came through, and he never told the bees, and that bothers him more than he can explain.
background_sections.now: He lives on Rootwater Isle, out where the swarms are thickest, and he wades through the reeds as if they were nothing. The climbers call him the beekeeper and send for him whenever something with a stinger is blocking the path. He always goes, and he always walks back. The venomancers say the poison likes him, but he says he's just calm, and he thinks those are the same thing.

recruits.look: Colombian man, 38, broad and strong, short black hair and beard, warm brown skin, dark eyes. Heavy dark green and gold beetle-shell armour, a thick wooden staff with a carved beetle head, a beekeeper's wide-brimmed hat with a mesh veil hanging down his back.

recruits.name: Clara Weiss
recruits.backstory: Clara read tree rings at the university in Freiburg. Give her a core the width of a pencil and she'll tell you every dry summer, every fire and every bad winter the tree lived through, four hundred years back. She came through on the ground and climbed the World Tree on purpose, because it's the biggest tree anyone has ever seen. It has no rings at all, and it's driving her mad. The grovekeepers say the tree heals people when it likes them, and it seems to like her.
recruits.greeting: This tree has no rings at all. I've taken cores in six places and there isn't a single ring anywhere. Sorry, hello, I'm Clara.

background_sections.before: Clara studied tree rings at the university in Freiburg. Give her a core the width of a pencil and she could tell you every dry summer, every fire and every bad winter a tree had lived through, four hundred years back. She worked in a tiny lab under the forestry building, with a wall of cores in labelled straws, and rode her bicycle up into the Black Forest every weekend. Once she dated a beam in an old farmhouse to a winter three hundred years ago, and the farmer cried.
background_sections.adjustment: She came through with her increment borer in her bag, which is the only reason anyone at Mossroof believes she was a scientist. She climbed the World Tree on purpose, because it's the biggest tree anyone has ever seen. The first time she put her hand on the bark to steady herself, the bark warmed under her palm, and a scratch on her wrist closed. The grovekeepers say the tree heals people when it likes them, and it seems to like her.
background_sections.forward: Clara wants to know how old the World Tree is, and she wants to know it properly, with evidence. She's tried six different methods so far and none of them has worked. After that, she'd like to tell her old department about it, mostly to see their faces. She suspects they wouldn't believe a word.
background_sections.now: She lives at Mossroof on the Lower Boughs, and she's usually sitting on the moss with her notebook open and her borer in her lap. The tree has no rings anywhere she's looked, and it's slowly driving her mad. She patches up climbers between measurements. She asks every one of them how high they've been, in case it helps.

recruits.look: German woman, 30, tall and slender, a honey-blonde braid over one shoulder, fair freckled skin, green eyes. Moss and woven-wood armour over soft leather, a living branch staff with fresh leaves, a slim metal tree-core drill in a sleeve on her hip.

recruits.name: Federico Lagos
recruits.backstory: Federico was a notary in Montevideo for nineteen years, in an office on Calle Sarandí with a brass seal, a fountain pen and a queue of people signing the biggest papers of their lives. He believes a promise is a contract and a contract is sacred, and he's never once broken his word. He came through on the ground and climbed the tree with a party that needed someone to hold the line, and he's held it ever since. The templars of Heartwatch watched the way he swears an oath and gave him a shield.
recruits.greeting: I've witnessed ten thousand promises, and I've learned to hear the ones people mean. Tell me what you need, and I'll tell you honestly whether I can promise it.

background_sections.before: Federico was a notary in Montevideo for nineteen years, in an office with green shutters on Calle Sarandi, with a brass seal, a fountain pen and a queue of people signing the biggest papers of their lives. His wife taught piano in the next room, and their grandson played with the seal on Saturdays. He read every contract aloud before anyone signed it, all of it, because he believed people deserved to know what they were promising. He has never once broken his word.
