background_sections.adjustment: He came through with his notary's seal in his pocket. He climbed the World Tree with a party that needed someone to hold the line, and he's held it ever since. The first time he promised to keep a stranger alive, light came up through his arm, and he kept that promise. The templars at Heartwatch saw the way he swore an oath and gave him a shield.
background_sections.forward: Federico wants to write the tree's first proper contract between the trolls and the climbers, and have both sides read it aloud before they sign. He also keeps a list of the promises he made at home and couldn't keep. He means to work through it, one way or another, and he hasn't told anyone what's at the top. He reads the whole list through every night before he sleeps.
background_sections.now: He stands at the gate of Heartwatch on the Middle Boughs with his shield and his seal. He still stamps the oaths the climbers swear there, and nobody has told him it doesn't count on this world. Every climber who leaves the camp promises to come back. He writes their names in a ledger and crosses them off when they return.

recruits.look: Uruguayan man, 42, tall and solid, dark hair greying at the temples, a trimmed grey-flecked beard, light olive skin, brown eyes. White and bronze templar plate engraved with oath-script, a tall rectangular shield and a flanged mace, a brass notary's seal on a chain at his belt.

recruits.name: Connor Walsh
recruits.backstory: Connor fished lobster off Inis Mór from the age of fourteen, in a boat his father built and a jumper his mother knitted, through every storm the Atlantic sent. He speaks Irish to the wind and English to people, and he's not sure which one listens better. He came through on the ground and climbed the tree to the top, because the higher he goes the more the weather feels like home. At Highrest the storm answers him, and the shamans say they've never seen anyone so happy about lightning.
recruits.greeting: That's a fine breeze up here. Back home we'd have called that a calm day and gone out for the pots.

background_sections.before: Connor fished for lobster off Inis Mor, the biggest of the Aran Islands, from the age of fourteen. He went out in a boat his father built, wearing a jumper his mother knitted, through every storm the Atlantic could send. He lived in a stone cottage at the end of a lane with a dog called Bran, and on Fridays there was a fiddle at the pub. His father taught him to read the sky before he could read a book, and the weather has never once caught him out.
background_sections.adjustment: He came through wearing his oilskins, which was lucky, because it was raining. He climbed the World Tree all the way to the top, because the higher he went, the more the weather felt like home. The first storm on the Upper Boughs knocked three climbers flat, and Connor stood in the middle of it laughing, with sparks running down his arms. The shamans say they've never seen anyone so happy about lightning.
background_sections.forward: Connor wants to sail something on this world, a skiff, a cloud, anything at all, out into weather nobody else will go near. He'd also like a decent pint, and he's told the trolls in great detail how to brew one. So far the results have been mixed. He drinks them anyway, out of politeness.
background_sections.now: He lives at Highrest on the Upper Boughs, out on the windward edge where nobody else will stand. He watches the storms roll across from the Stormsplit and tells the camp which ones to worry about, and he hasn't been wrong yet. He speaks Irish to the wind and English to people. He's not sure which of them listens better.

recruits.look: Irish man, 35, broad and strong, windswept red-brown hair and a short beard, fair weathered skin, blue-grey eyes. Shaman mail over a thick cream knitted jumper, two fist-axes with sparks on the blades, a yellow oilskin fisherman's hat tied to his belt.

recruits.name: Mauricio Peña
recruits.backstory: Mauricio ran his family's funeral home in Guadalajara for twenty-two years, and every Day of the Dead he built the biggest altar in the barrio, with marigolds from the door to the street. He's gentle with the grieving and funny with everyone else, and death has never frightened him. He woke on a cloud above the World Tree, decided he'd died, and took it very well. The survey found him and kept him as a guest, and it turns out the dead still listen to him.
recruits.greeting: When I woke up on a cloud, I assumed I'd died, and I was very pleased with the arrangements. Then a man with crystal on his face asked me to fill in a form.

background_sections.before: Mauricio ran his family's funeral home in Guadalajara for twenty-two years, in a building with blue tiles and a hearse he washed every morning. His wife sang at the services, and their three daughters wouldn't touch the business. Every Day of the Dead he built the biggest altar in the barrio, with marigolds from the door to the street. Every November he walked the whole neighbourhood with a cart of marigolds and gave them away to anyone who wanted them.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke up on a cloud above the World Tree, decided he must have died, and took it very well. The Aetherian survey found him and wrote him down as a ward, then asked him a great many questions about funerals. He answered every one of them at length, with diagrams. The first time something died near him on the cloud, he felt it go, so he asked it politely to stay a while, and it did.
background_sections.forward: Mauricio wants to build an altar on this world, a proper one, for everyone who came through and everyone they left behind. He'd like marigolds for it, and he's asked the survey's gardeners to find him something orange. So far they've brought him four different flowers, and none of them is right. He's keeping all four anyway.
background_sections.now: He's at the Annex on the Sunward Crown with the survey's other guests from Earth, keeping the peace between them. He's gentle with the grieving and funny with everyone else, and death has never frightened him. The Earthborn come to him when somebody's grieving. The Aetherians come to him when they want to understand why.

recruits.look: Mexican man, 41, tall and broad, slicked-back black hair, a neat moustache and short beard, warm brown skin, dark eyes. Heavy black and bone-white reaper armour with silver skulls, a long scythe, an orange marigold pinned at his collar.

recruits.name: Étienne Gagnon
recruits.backstory: Étienne drove the Zamboni at a hockey rink in Montréal's east end for ten years, and the players said his ice was like glass. He played in a beer league on Tuesdays, coached a peewee team on Saturdays and never missed a Canadiens game. He woke on a sky island in a snowdrift, which felt like home until he looked over the edge. The survey brought him to the Annex, and the cold has come when he calls it ever since.
recruits.greeting: Back home I made ice for a living, and I was very good at it. Up here, it turns out, I still am.

background_sections.before: Etienne drove the ice resurfacer at a hockey rink in Montreal's east end for ten years, and the players said his ice was like glass. He lived in a walk-up in Hochelaga, played in a beer league on Tuesdays and coached a peewee team on Saturdays that never won a single game. He never missed a Canadiens match. Every morning at six he flooded the ice, slow and even, and he loved the quiet before anyone else came in. He wore a toque his grandmother had knitted him, winter and summer.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke up in a snowdrift on a sky island, which felt like home until he looked over the edge. The Aetherian survey brought him to the Annex, and the cold has come whenever he calls it ever since. The first time he frosted a cup of water without trying, the Aetherians decided he must be a weather mage. He told them he drove a Zamboni, and it took an hour to explain what that was. He practised on a pond until he could freeze it so flat and clear you could see the fish.
background_sections.forward: Etienne wants to build a proper rink on this world and teach somebody to skate, a troll or an Aetherian or anyone willing to try. He's already picked out a spot. After that, he'd like to know whether his peewees ever won a game without him. He likes to think they did, at least once.
background_sections.now: He's at the Annex on the Sunward Crown now, keeping the survey's water cold and the Earthborn guests' spirits up. He's flooded a corner of the cloud into a small rink. On quiet evenings the guests go round it in their boots, falling over and laughing. He stands at the edge and gives them advice they don't take.

recruits.look: French-Canadian man, 32, athletic, dark-blond hair short with a little length on top, light stubble, fair skin, blue eyes. Ice-blue and white frost-mage robes with a fur collar, a staff topped with a clear ice crystal, a red and white knitted toque.

recruits.name: Oliver Hayes
recruits.backstory: Oliver ran a small optician's in Clifton for eleven years, with a test chart, a cardigan and a kettle that never got a rest. He's kind, careful and a little shy, and he can't walk past a pair of glasses that need adjusting. He woke on a sky island with his spectacles still on, and the House of the Patient Lens has thought him the most interesting man in the sky ever since. At Lenswatch the light listens to him, and he's learned to put it where people hurt.
recruits.greeting: Follow my finger, please. Sorry, it's a habit, because the survey has me looking at everyone's eyes, including their own.

background_sections.before: Oliver ran a small optician's shop in Clifton, in Bristol, for eleven years, with a test chart, a cardigan and a kettle that never got a rest. The shop had a green door on a steep street, and a cat that slept in the frames display. He sang in a choir on Thursday nights. Once, during a routine test, he spotted something serious behind a schoolboy's eye, and the boy's mother sent him a card every Christmas after that.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke on a sky island with his spectacles still on, and the House of the Patient Lens has thought him the most interesting man in the sky ever since. On his first day at Lenswatch, the lensmaster sat him down and asked him about eyes for nine hours straight. Oliver answered every question and then asked for a cup of tea. The light came to him the first time he held a lens up to a wounded guard, and it went straight through the glass and into the wound.
background_sections.forward: Oliver wants to make a proper pair of glasses for an Aetherian, whose eyes glow, which nobody has ever tried. He's made four attempts so far, and the lenses keep cracking in the light. He'd also like his cardigan back. He knows that isn't going to happen.
background_sections.now: He works in the survey's workshop at Lenswatch, grinding lenses with the lensmaster and arguing happily about light. Once a week he checks the eyes of the other guests from Earth, because nobody else up here knows how. He's kind, careful and a little shy. He can't walk past a pair of glasses that need adjusting.

recruits.look: English man, 36, tall and slim, neatly parted light-brown hair, clean-shaven, fair skin, hazel eyes behind round wire spectacles. White and gold sun-cleric robes with a gold sun disc, a slim staff topped with a glowing sun, a pen-torch clipped in his breast pocket.

recruits.name: Tariq Al-Jubouri
recruits.backstory: Tariq lifted weights for Iraq at two Asian Games, coached boys at a gym in Karrada after he retired, and gave blood every eight weeks from the day he turned eighteen. He's enormous, softly spoken and kinder than anyone expects, and he doesn't like to hurry. He woke on a sky island north of Aurelion and lifted a fallen cart off an Aetherian child before anyone had asked his name. The houses took him in as a guest, and the blood he gave all those years seems to know him here.
recruits.greeting: I gave blood every eight weeks for twenty years, and here it seems the blood remembers. It gives a little back now. Please, take your time, there's no hurry.

background_sections.before: Tariq lifted weights for Iraq at two Asian Games, and when he retired he coached boys at a gym in Karrada with a tin roof and a fan that never worked. He covered one wall with photographs of the boys he'd trained, and he knew every one of their stories. His wife Nadia made the best kubba on their street, and their daughter Zainab could lift more than half his students. From the day he turned eighteen he gave blood every eight weeks. The nurse at the blood bank knew him by name and always gave him two biscuits instead of one.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke up on a sky island north of Aurelion and, before anyone had even asked his name, lifted a fallen cart off an Aetherian child. The Aetherians had never seen anyone lift that much, and the Ascendancy asked him to join them within a week. He said no, very politely, because he didn't like the way they talked about people. The first time he was cut in a fight, the blood didn't run out of him. It stopped, and then it pulled him back up onto his feet.
background_sections.forward: Tariq wants to open a gym here for anyone at all, Aetherian, troll or Earthborn, with a fan that actually works. He wants it to be the kind of place his old gym was, where nobody gets turned away and nobody gets hurried. He'd like to keep the Ascendancy's recruiters out of it, too. And one day he'd like to have someone to hand two biscuits to, the way the nurse always did for him.
background_sections.now: These days he lives at the Ground Embassy in Aurelion, where the council houses its guests from the ground. He carries things for the embassy staff whether they ask him to or not. The city's guards have started training with him in the mornings, and they've stopped laughing at how slowly he does everything. He's noticed the Ascendancy's recruiters watching his trainees, and he doesn't like it one bit.

recruits.look: Iraqi man, 39, very big and powerfully built, short black hair, a full short black beard, warm brown skin, dark eyes. Heavy crimson and black bloodmage plate with blood-red runes, a rune-marked shield and a broad sword, a faint red mist round his free hand, a thick worn leather weightlifting belt.

recruits.name: Isabela Moura
recruits.backstory: Isabela blew glass in a workshop on the lagoon at Florianópolis, bowls and lamps and fish for the tourists, and once a chandelier for a church that took her a whole summer. She's bright, chatty and enchanted by almost everything, and she's proud of the burn scars on both forearms. She woke on a sky island beside a crystal that was humming, and when she touched it, it sang. The Aetherians brought her to Aurelion to find out why, and they're still finding out.
recruits.greeting: The whole city sings when you touch it, did you know that? Put your hand on the wall and try it.

background_sections.before: Isabela blew glass in a workshop on the lagoon at Florianopolis, in Brazil, making bowls, lamps and little glass fish for the tourists. Once she spent a whole summer making a chandelier for a church. Her workshop doors stood open to the lagoon, and her furnace never went out. She could tell the heat of the glass to within a few degrees by its colour, and she never used a thermometer. Her brother surfed all day and never once helped.
background_sections.adjustment: She woke on a sky island next to a humming crystal, and when she touched it, it sang. The Aetherian who found her went pale and sent for three scholars. They brought her to Aurelion to find out why the crystal answers her, and they're still trying. The Academy taught her arcane magic in a single season, because she already knew how to shape something that glows.
background_sections.forward: Isabela wants to blow a lamp out of Aetherian crystal, which nobody here has ever managed, because they only know how to cut it. She's ruined eleven pieces trying so far. She'd also love for her brother to see the city one day. She's sure it would finally impress him.
background_sections.now: She works in Aurelion now, near the Academies on the Inner Ring, and she puts her hands on every wall she passes. The magisters let her use a corner of the Academy workshops, and the crystal hums whenever she walks in. She's bright and chatty and enchanted by almost everything. She's proud of the burn scars on both her forearms.

recruits.look: Brazilian woman, 31, slim and graceful, long loose wavy dark-brown hair, warm light-brown skin, brown eyes. Violet and white arcane-mage robes with glowing crystal trim, a staff of clear blown glass with violet light inside, tinted glassblower's glasses pushed up into her hair.

recruits.name: Renata Rojas
recruits.backstory: Renata was a stunt double in Mexico City for nine years, the woman who fell off buildings, out of cars and down stairs so the stars didn't have to. She's fearless, funny and very good at falling, and she'll do any fall twice if the first take wasn't clean. She woke on a sky island right on the edge and nearly went over before she'd opened her eyes. The Aetherians found her climbing their skiff rigging for fun, and the Expanse's long drops feel like work to her, in a good way.
recruits.greeting: People keep warning me about the edge. I've jumped off taller things for less money, and I always land.

background_sections.before: Renata was a stunt double in Mexico City for nine years, the woman who fell off buildings, out of cars and down stairs so the stars didn't have to. She lived in a rooftop flat in Roma Norte with a crash mat in the living room. For a telenovela finale she did a high fall off the roof of a hotel, and the director made her do it twice. Her mother refused to watch a single one of her films.
background_sections.adjustment: She woke on a sky island right at the edge and nearly went over before she'd even opened her eyes. The Aetherians wrote her down as a ward who kept escaping, which she thinks was unfair, because she always came back. They found her climbing their skiff rigging for fun. She learned to use blades from an Earthborn who used to be a chef, and she learned the rest by falling off islands and catching herself.
background_sections.forward: Renata wants to dive off the edge of the Expanse into the cloud and come up somewhere else, just once, on purpose. She'd love somebody to film it, and she knows that's the hard part. Nobody up here has ever heard of a camera. She's thought about describing it to an Aetherian painter instead.
background_sections.now: She lives in the Celestial Expanse now, out on the edges where the falls pour off, walking the rims as if they were pavements. She runs messages between the islands faster than the skiffs, and she never takes the bridges. The Expanse's long drops feel like work to her, in a good way. She'll do any fall twice if the first one wasn't clean.

recruits.look: Mexican woman, 29, athletic and lithe, long dark-brown hair in a high ponytail, golden-tan skin, dark eyes. Fitted dark leather rogue armour with a short hooded cape, two short swords, black fingerless stunt gloves and a red bandana tied round one wrist.

recruits.name: Raúl Castillo
recruits.backstory: Raúl rode bulls on the rodeo circuit out of Tucson for fifteen years, and he's got a silver buckle for every one he won and a scar for every one he didn't. He's loud, cocky and better company than he lets on, and he's never met a horse he couldn't talk round. He came through on the ground and climbed the tree because someone told him the trolls up there respect a man who keeps his trophies. They do, and the headhunters of the Great Settlement adopted him in a week.
recruits.greeting: Eight seconds is a long time on a bull, friend. Up here, I've learned it's a long time on a raptor too.

background_sections.before: Raul rode bulls on the rodeo circuit out of Tucson for fifteen years, and he has a silver buckle for every ride he won and a scar for every one he didn't. He lived in a trailer with a pickup out front and a saddle worth more than the trailer. His mother never once watched him ride. She kept every buckle on a shelf in her kitchen anyway, polished, with the dates written underneath.
background_sections.adjustment: He came through wearing his biggest buckle, the national one, and the first troll who saw it tried to buy it from him. He climbed the World Tree because somebody told him the trolls up there respect a man who keeps his trophies. In his first month he rode a raptor on a dare and stayed on for nine seconds, and the headhunters still talk about it. They adopted him within a week.
background_sections.forward: Raul wants to ride a wild wyvern off the Upper Boughs and stay on. After that, he'd like to win something on this world worth putting on a shelf. He's never said who the shelf would be for. Everyone who knows him can guess.
background_sections.now: He lives in the Great Settlement, and he's usually in the middle of the market, polishing his buckle and arguing about technique with any headhunter who'll stop. He's loud and cocky and better company than he lets on. The headhunters have hung his old rodeo number among their trophies. He pretends he isn't proud of it.

recruits.look: Mexican-American man, 36, broad-shouldered and lean, a short dark beard, warm tan skin, brown eyes, a battered tan brim hat. Barbarian furs and leathers with bone beads, two short war axes, trophy charms at his belt, a big polished silver rodeo buckle.

recruits.name: Facundo Herrera
recruits.backstory: Facundo repaired watches in Mendoza for twenty years in his grandfather's shop, under a sign nobody had repainted in half a century. He can strip a pocket watch to its last screw and put it back together blindfold, and he's the most patient man anyone in the Expanse has met. He woke on a sky island with his loupe round his neck and his grandfather's watch still ticking. The Aetherians found him, and up here he can wind time back a little on a wound.
recruits.greeting: Everything runs a little slow or a little fast if you listen closely. Your heart's running quick, by the way, so sit down for a minute.

background_sections.before: Facundo repaired watches in Mendoza for twenty years, in his grandfather's narrow shop between a bakery and a shoe repairer, under a sign nobody had repainted in fifty years. He worked at a bench by the window, beneath a wall of clocks that all struck noon a few seconds apart. His grandfather taught him never to force a watch, but to listen to it until it told him what was wrong. He can strip a pocket watch to its last screw and put it back together blindfold.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke on a sky island with his loupe round his neck and his grandfather's watch still ticking in his pocket. The Aetherian scholars found it so interesting that they took it apart, and he made them put it back together in front of him. The first time he held a bleeding man's wrist, he felt the moment slip under his fingers. He wound it back a few seconds, and the cut wasn't there any more.
background_sections.forward: Facundo wants to understand the golems' cores, because they're the most beautiful mechanisms he's ever seen. He's taken notes on three of them and understands about a tenth of what he's found. He'd also like to know whether his grandfather's watch is keeping the same time as the clocks at home. He suspects it isn't, and he winds it anyway.
background_sections.now: He lives in the Celestial Expanse now, among the fallen golems, sitting cross-legged with his loupe in his eye. He tends the wounded who come back off the Golem Fields. He's the most patient man anyone in the Expanse has ever met. He winds his grandfather's watch every morning at exactly the same minute.

recruits.look: Argentine man, 37, medium build and fit, swept-back dark-brown hair, a short neat beard, light olive skin, brown eyes. Bronze and sand-gold chronomancer robes with clockwork motifs, a staff topped with a glowing hourglass, a jeweller's loupe on a cord and a gold pocket-watch chain.

recruits.name: Rhodri Evans
recruits.backstory: Rhodri propped for Pontypridd on Saturdays for fifteen years and put up scaffolding the rest of the week, from terraced streets in the valleys to the walls of Caerphilly Castle. Nobody got past him on the pitch, and nobody ever fell off anything he built. He woke on the Waking Shore last spring with his boots full of sand, and by the afternoon he was carrying poles up to Amberwatch. The night the naga came up the beach, fire came up through him to meet them, and the Conclave's magisters have been arguing about what to call it ever since.
recruits.greeting: Mind your head, that pole's not tied off yet. I've had scaffolding up the side of Caerphilly Castle, so one broken gatehouse isn't going to frighten me.

background_sections.before: Rhodri played prop for Pontypridd on Saturdays for fifteen years and put up scaffolding the rest of the week, from terraced streets in the Welsh valleys to the walls of Caerphilly Castle. He had a van with his name on the side and a crew of four lads from his own street. He clipped every one of them on before they climbed, every single time. Nobody got past him on the pitch, and nobody ever fell off anything he built.
background_sections.adjustment: He woke on Dawnhaven's Waking Shore last spring with his boots full of sand, and by the afternoon he was carrying poles up to Amberwatch. For the first week he couldn't understand a word the elves said, and he took that better than most, because half the valleys can't follow him either. The night the naga came up the beach, fire rose up through him to meet them. The Conclave's magisters have been arguing about what to call it ever since.
background_sections.forward: Rhodri wants Amberwatch roofed before the first proper storm, then the walls at Firstlight Spire, and then whatever comes next. He'd also love a game, fifteen a side on a flat bit of grass, with anyone daft enough to pack down against him. He's been teaching a few of the elves the rules. They think it's barbaric, and they keep coming back.
background_sections.now: He works at Amberwatch in Amberleaf Glade, up the scaffolding on the old gatehouse with a hammer in his belt and a pole on his shoulder. What gets to him is the quiet, with no match on a Saturday, no singing on the terrace and no lads. He fills it by building, because a roof going up sounds the same on any world. When there's trouble on the cove road he climbs down and stands at the front, and then he goes back up to finish the joint he was working on.

recruits.look: Welsh man, 38, big, broad and solid, a thick ginger beard, short reddish hair, fair weathered skin, blue eyes. Heavy crimson plate with dark iron edges and a glowing red sigil, a sword and a tall red shield.

recruits.name: Yiannis Papadakis
recruits.backstory: Yiannis dived for octopus off Chania from the age of nine and beat them soft on the harbour stones for the tavernas. He sings to the sea when it's rough, and he has since he was sixteen. He woke in the surf of the Waking Shore two years ago, before the Conclave had a tent up, and the first person he pulled out after that was an elf girl who wasn't breathing. Light came into his hands while he worked on her, and she breathed. He's kept the shore ever since.
recruits.greeting: Ela, come up out of the water, my friend, slowly. You're on Dawnhaven, the sea brought you, and the sea brings everybody here eventually.

background_sections.before:
A blue boat in the old harbour at Chania, a wife who could out-argue a bishop, and two daughters, one bound for Athens and one bound for the sea.

His grandfather fished those waters and so did his father. He was the careful one, and he had good reason to be.
background_sections.adjustment:
He talks to his wife and his girls every night, out loud, on the beach, and he doesn't care who hears him.

The Conclave's priests asked where he learned to call the Light. He told them on a harbour wall, with a child who wasn't breathing, and they stopped asking.
background_sections.forward:
He wants nobody the sea gives up on his shore to be lost, ever.

One day he'd like to sing a song he hasn't sung in thirty years, out loud, for somebody who isn't here to hear it.
background_sections.now:
Amberleaf Glade, on the Waking Shore, up to his knees in the surf.

Whoever the sea gives up, he wades in and gets them, wraps them in a blanket and sings them a couplet about how they looked coming out of the water. The rangers bring him their wounded, because the Light comes when he asks.

recruits.look: Greek man, 47, broad and solid, thick salt-and-pepper beard and hair, olive skin, dark eyes. White and gold plate with a sun on the chest, a round gold shield and a mace, a flat cap.

recruits.name: Leif Halvorsen
recruits.backstory: Leif spent twenty-five years in the Oregon woods as a faller and a tree climber, and he loves trees more than anybody you'll meet. He came down out of a gold tree in Ashenvale three years ago, and the forest woke up in him the same week, which he thinks is either a joke or a sentence. When the Conclave sent word round Azshara for somebody who knew wood, he got on the boat. Now he brings in deadwood for Dawnrest, and only deadwood.
recruits.greeting: Watch where you stand. That old red one's got a dead limb up top that's been thinking about coming down all week.

background_sections.before: Leif grew up in Coos Bay, Oregon, where everybody's dad worked in timber. His grandfather came over from Norway to work the mills, but Leif went up the trees instead, and spent twenty-five years as a faller and a tree climber without ever falling once. He loves trees more than anybody you'll ever meet. His daughter fights wildfires, and his pickup always smelled of saw oil and coffee.
background_sections.adjustment: He came down out of a golden tree in Ashenvale three years ago, and the forest woke up inside him the same week. He thinks that's either a joke or a sentence. He spent two years with the druids in Ashenvale learning that the forest would rather he didn't cut it, and he hasn't started a saw since. When the elves of Dawnhaven wanted him to fell the old red trees for their beams, he took one look and showed them what was already lying on the ground.
background_sections.forward: Leif wants to understand why the woods picked him, of all people. After that, he'd like to spend one morning in an old stand of trees with nothing to do but look at them. He's never had a morning like that in his life. He's starting to think he's earned one.
background_sections.now: When the Conclave sent word round for somebody who knew wood, he got on the boat to Dawnhaven. Now he works in Duskfall Woods, in the Red Hollow, hauling deadwood out to the road for Dawnrest's roof, and only deadwood. The bears in the hollow mostly leave him alone. He always looks up before he steps under anything, and he'll tell you to do the same.

recruits.look: American man, 46, big and broad, a thick sandy-grey beard and long tied-back hair, weathered fair skin, blue eyes. Red and green plaid under worn leather and fur, a pair of axes, braces and heavy boots.
